standard_prerequisites.name: At-worst-nodal schemes of relative dimension one over a discrete valuation ring, and blowing up a closed point
standard_prerequisites.statement: A scheme of relative dimension one over a discrete valuation ring is at-worst-nodal when its singularities are ordinary double points with smooth branches, so that in a neighbourhood of a singular point it is described by a product of a smooth curve germ with a standard node over the ring; the singular points of the special fibre are then finite in number and are exactly the singular points of the total space up to a local computation. Blowing up a closed point replaces it by the projectivised normal cone, and the chapter proves that the blowing up of a singular point remains at-worst-nodal of relative dimension one, that this operation is compatible with the étale local description of the node and with base change to a further blowing up. The author's own lemmas and examples of the same chapter, and the results of the Algebra, Curves, Divisors and Morphisms chapters that the proof quotes, are the allowed inputs.
standard_prerequisites.use: The counted lemma is the resolution step that the chapter uses to pass from an at-worst-nodal model to a regular one in the semistable reduction section.

core_obligations: Reduce to finitely many singular points: quasi-compactness passes to the special fibre, whose singularities are at-worst-nodal, so the fibre has finitely many nodes and is smooth elsewhere; the singular points of the total space are therefore finite in number and each lies over a node (source lines 6216-6230).

Describe the neighbourhood of a node: around a singular point the scheme is étale locally a standard node over the ring, a description the chapter records together with its compatibility under postcomposition with an étale map, and this description is what makes the following blowup computation local (source lines 6230-6260).

Blow up one singular point: blowing up a singular closed point resolves that point, keeps the scheme at-worst-nodal of relative dimension one over the ring, and produces a scheme whose singular points are again finite; the effect on the number of singular points is computed in the étale local model (source lines 6260-6296).

Iterate and terminate: the blowup of one singular point is compatible with the local description and with a further blowup, so the operations can be carried out in a compatible sequence whose length is half the number of singular points, after which the scheme has one singular point fewer; induction on the number of singular points finishes the resolution (source lines 6296-6309).

proof_roadmap.step: Finiteness of the singular points via quasi-compactness and the at-worst-nodal assumption.
The étale local description of a node and its compatibility with further étale maps.
The blowup of a singular closed point in the local model, keeping the class of the scheme.
The compatible sequence of blowups, the drop in the number of singular points and the induction.
